summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes and a history of gastroparesis was admitted for intractable nausea and vomiting, unable to tolerate oral intake. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and antiemetics including ondansetron, prochlorperazine, metoclopramide, and lorazepam. Her elevated blood glucose and ketonuria suggested mild diabetic ketoacidosis, which resolved with insulin and hydration. Hypertension and tachycardia, likely secondary to dehydration and vomiting, improved with IV fluids and resumed oral antihypertensives. She gradually advanced to a soft diet, tolerated oral intake, and returned to her baseline. A urine culture showed contamination, not infection. She was discharged home with instructions to continue her regular medications and follow up with her primary care provider and endocrinologist.
